record.question: In Windows OS, the Recycle Bin does not store files deleted from
record.explanation: D is the uniquely best printed choice under normal Windows deletion behavior: files on removable USB flash media bypass the Windows Recycle Bin. Desktop and Documents on a local fixed volume, and the ordinary internal disk, support recycling. The term removable matters: USB is a connection interface, and an externally connected disk can be classified as fixed and have a Recycle Bin. Arbitrary Shift+Delete, capacity limits, or custom settings can also bypass recycling elsewhere, but the stem gives no such exceptional operation and those possibilities do not make A–C equally good category answers. Precision note: This answer concerns ordinary deletion from removable USB flash media. USB-attached disks classified as fixed may have a Recycle Bin; USB attachment alone does not decide the behavior. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://explorerplusplus.readthedocs.io/en/latest/menus/file/delete.html; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getdrivetypew; https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management/commands/management/ClearRecycleBinCommand.cs
